parole.significato: the flesh side of split leather (haljasnahka)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haljas, borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian zaļš, Lithuanian žãlias).

parole.significato: fork (of a tree and its branch, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hanka, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian atšanka with an extra prefix).
From Proto-Finnic *habën, possibly a Baltic loan.
From Proto-Finnic *hirmu (compare Estonian hirm, Livonian irm), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian širmuļi, Lithuanian šiurpus). Probably also related to hirveä.
From Proto-Finnic *hooli (compare Estonian hool, Ingrian hooli, Karelian huoli), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian žala (“damage, harm”)).

parole.significato: porridge (especially one made of flour as opposed to groats), gruel
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huttu, possibly an old past passive participle of a verb borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian šusti (“to stew”)). Cognate to Karelian huttu, Ludian huttu. May also be related to Proto-Permic *šu̇d (“soup”), if it is derived from the same Baltic root.
From Proto-Finnic *härkä (compare Estonian härg), probably borrowed from Baltic. * (Taurus): Semantic loan from Latin taurus. * (Ox in the Chinese zodiac): Semantic loan from Chinese 牛宿 (Niúxiù).
From Proto-Finnic *joutadak, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian jaudāt).
From Proto-Finnic *kampi, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kampas). Doublet of kamppi.
From Proto-Finnic *kappalëh ~ *kapalëh (compare Livonian kabāl), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian gabals (“piece”), Lithuanian gabalas), somewhat nativized with the -e suffix.

parole.significato: cranberry (shrub belonging to the section Vaccinium sect. Oxycoccus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karpa-(la-) (compare Karelian karpalo, Kukkuzi karpolo, Livonian gārban, Livvi garbalo, Veps garbal), possibly from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *karta, borrowed from a Baltic or Germanic language. Cognates include Estonian kard and Ingrian karta.

parole.significato: hair (single hair on human or animal) (not used of human head hair except in a technical sense)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karva (compare Estonian karv, Livonian kǭra, Veps karv), borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian gaũras). In the first texts, karva is attested only in the sense “color”; in its current meaning, it is first mentioned in a biblical text in 1621. Displaced in the sense “color” by v
From Proto-Finnic *kiirek, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian šķire, Lithuanian skỹris).

From Proto-Finnic *kirpedä, derived from a root borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kirpti); according to EVE, the adjective may be a back-formation from the now dialectal verb kirventää, which would derive from Baltic.

Somehow from Proto-Finnic *kurdëh ~ *kurnëh ~ *kurnës (difficult to reconstruct due to seemingly irregular sound changes, but compare dialectal kuurne, Estonian kurt, Karelian kuurnis, Ludian kuurniž, Veps kurdiž, Võro kurt'), probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian kurls (“deaf”) and Lithuan

parole.significato: ripe, mature, matured (ready for reaping or use)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küpci, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian cepts; see Proto-Finnic entry for more). The inflection type has been analogically remodelled; earlier inflection kypsi (genitive kypsen, partitive kystä) still survives in some dialects, usually as a noun. In others, the parti
From Proto-Finnic *lakso, possibly borrowed from Baltic. Related to Ingrian laksu, Karelian lakšu and Veps laks.

parole.significato: thin, lean, meagre, slim, skinny (of a human or animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laiha (compare Estonian lahja), borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian liesas).

parole.significato: shovel (tool for moving portions of material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lapido (compare Estonian labidas, Livvi labju, Veps labid), probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian lópeta (“shovel”), Old Prussian lopto (“spade”)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: blaze (white or lighter-coloured markings on a horse's face)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laukki, probably borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: jaw (part of the face below the mouth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëuka, possibly borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: to blow air on a fire or embers (to make them burn better or at a higher temperature)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëëccodak (compare Estonian lõõtsuma), from *lëëcca, possibly of Baltic origin.

parole.significato: flood meadow, swamp (a low-lying meadow subject to seasonal flooding; intermittently flooded meadow)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luhta, borrowed from a Baltic language, compare Lithuanian lukštas (“Caltha palustris”).
From Proto-Finnic *luuta (compare Ludian luud and Veps lud), borrowed from a Baltic language (compare Latvian slota, Lithuanian šlúota).

parole.significato: bride (woman in the context of her own wedding)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *morcijan, borrowed from Baltic; compare Lithuanian marti (“daughter-in-law”), Old Prussian martin (“bride, sister-in-law”) (accusative singular). Cognates in other Finnic languages include Estonian mõrsja (“bride”), Ingrian morssia (“bride”), Karelian moršien (“bride”), Veps murze
From Proto-Finnic *muli, probably borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: damp, not quite wet nor dry
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näivä (compare Karelian näivälleh, Veps näivištuda), probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian naivà, neivà).

parole.significato: rod, pole (long, thin object such as a fishing rod)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pahla, probably borrowed from Baltic.

From Proto-Finnic *paimën, borrowed from a Baltic language (compare Lithuanian piemuo), from Proto-Indo-European *poh₂imḗn (compare Ancient Greek ποιμήν (poimḗn)), from *peh₂- (“to protect”) (compare Latin pastor). Related to Karelian paimoi.
From Proto-Finnic *pëlu, borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian pélūs).

From Proto-Finnic *perkeleh, which derives from the name of the Baltic deity of thunder; compare Lithuanian Perkūnas and Proto-Slavic *Perunъ (“god of thunder”). After Finland's conquest (c. 1250) and subsequent Christianization, its meaning changed to a profanity and a euphemism for Satan at least

parole.significato: dry weather; a weather without rain, snow or any other precipitation, and which may be sunny or cloudy
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pouta, possibly borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *ragënta, from Baltic.

parole.significato: hole (relatively small and/or shallow hole that goes through something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raika (compare Veps reig), possibly borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *raici (compare Estonian reis), borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian rietas (“thigh”)).

parole.significato: sleigh (vehicle, generally pulled by an animal, which moves over snow or ice on runners, used for transporting persons…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *reki (compare Estonian regi), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian ragavas, Lithuanian ragės).

parole.significato: thread (long, thin and flexible form of material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rihma, from earlier *rišma, borrowed from a Baltic language, compare Lithuanian rišimas (“binding”). Cognate with Estonian rihm, Karelian rihma, Votic rihmõ.
From Proto-Finnic *salo, probably borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: wall (substantial structure acting as side or division in a building; something with the apparent solidity and dimensio…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *saina (compare Estonian sein), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian siena (“wall”)).
From Proto-Finnic *siipi, possibly a Baltic loan. Cognates include Estonian tiib, Ingrian siipi, Karelian šiipi /šiibi, Livonian tībõz, Livvi siibi, Ludian siib, Veps šīb, Võro siib, Votic siipi.

parole.significato: salt (common table salt, sodium chloride, NaCl)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soola (compare Estonian sool, Veps sol), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian sāls), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sḗh₂l. Words of Indo-European origin occur also in many other Uralic languages (compare Erzya сал (sal), Udmurt сылал (sylal), Komi-Permyak сов (sov)); while
From Proto-Finnic *sünkedä (compare Karelian synkie), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian sunkùs (“heavy”)).

parole.significato: hide, fleece (prepared skin of an animal, still with hair or fur)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talja, possibly borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: amadou; fine-grained tinder made from a polypore of species Fomes fomentarius
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *takla (compare Estonian tael, Karelian takla, Votic taglõ), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian dagla, Lithuanian deglis).

parole.significato: black grouse, Lyrurus tetrix, formerly Tetrao tetrix
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tetri, possibly a Baltic loan. Cognate with Estonian teder.
From Proto-Finnic *tolma, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian dulkti).
From Proto-Finnic *toohi (compare Estonian toht, Ingrian toohi), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian tāss).
From Proto-Finnic *toorëh, borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian dõras (“good”)).
From Proto-Finnic *uksi, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian uoksas (“hole”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vëhmas, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian vešùmas).
From Proto-Finnic *vik'at'ëh (compare Estonian vikat, Veps vikateh, Votic vikahtõ), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian izkapts).
From Proto-Finnic *virpa, borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian virbs, Lithuanian vir̃bas).

parole.significato: goat, Capra hircus, syn. Capra aegagrus hircus (domestic goat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voohi (compare Ingrian voohi, Votic voho), borrowed from a Baltic language (compare Latvian āzis, Lithuanian ožys, Old Prussian wosee).
From Proto-Finnic *vootna. Related to Ingrian voonna, Karelian vuonu, Veps vodnaz and Votic võdnõ. Possibly derived from *vooci, or borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *äges, possibly borrowed from a Baltic language, compare Lithuanian akečios. Cognate to Estonian äke and Veps ägez.
